overview: Two of the most feared non-fermenting Gram-negative rods in hospital-acquired infection, distinguished at the bench by a single simple test.
genZNote: Two non-fermenters hospitals really don't want to see on a culture.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A motile, oxidase-positive non-fermenter, often producing a blue-green pigment (pyocyanin) and a grape-like odor.
aspects.valueB: A non-motile, oxidase-negative coccobacillus notorious for surviving on dry hospital surfaces and acquiring resistance genes.

aspects.label: Motility
aspects.valueA: Motile via a single polar flagellum.

aspects.label: Pigment / Odor
aspects.valueA: Often produces blue-green pyocyanin pigment and a sweet, grape-like odor.
aspects.valueB: Typically non-pigmented, without a distinctive odor.

aspects.label: Environmental Resilience
aspects.valueA: Thrives in moist environments (sinks, respiratory equipment, water systems).
aspects.valueB: Notably resilient on dry surfaces, allowing prolonged survival and outbreak potential in ICUs.

aspects.label: Key Resistance Concern
aspects.valueA: Intrinsic resistance plus efflux pumps and inducible AmpC; can develop carbapenem resistance via porin loss/efflux.
aspects.valueB: Rapidly acquires resistance genes, frequently reaching extensively drug-resistant (XDR) or pandrug-resistant status via carbapenemases.

aspects.label: Typical Infections
aspects.valueA: Ventilator-associated pneumonia, burn wound infections, cystic fibrosis chronic lung infection.
aspects.valueB: Ventilator-associated pneumonia and bloodstream infections, especially in trauma and burn units and after prolonged ICU stays.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueB: Oxidase-negative, non-motile, notorious for surface persistence and rapid resistance acquisition.
